disclosures.name: TestCopyError
disclosures.signature: pre-conn.Close, expected handler to still be running
disclosures.reason: the test's own instrument is a full-process goroutine dump: handlerRunning() calls runtime.Stack(buf, true) and regexp-matches `net/http/cgi\.\(\*Handler\)\.ServeHTTP` in it, i.e. it asks the runtime to render ANOTHER goroutine's frames and then greps them. That facility is defined over the replaced runtime's own internals -- Go walks every g's saved stack through its scheduler; the CLR has no supported way to walk another thread's stack, so runtime.Stack's `all` parameter degrades by documented design to the calling thread's own trace (src/core/runtime/managed_impl.cs: "all=true reports only the calling thread -- the CLR has no supported way to walk another thread's stack"). The probe is therefore false for a handler running on any other thread, and the first assert -- the pre-conn.Close liveness check pinned here -- fails before the test reaches the behavior it was written to measure. A truthful managed rendering of a foreign thread's Go frames does not exist at any cost, and synthesizing a plausible ServeHTTP frame into the dump would pass this regexp while proving nothing about whether any handler is running, which is fabrication rather than implementation; the row is pinned as failing for that reason. The behavior actually under test -- Handler.ServeHTTP detecting a copy error and killing the CGI child rather than blocking forever on exec.Cmd.Wait -- is proven independently, on the same run, by the passing sibling TestKillChildAfterCopyError (integration_test.go:93), which drives the identical path through a limitWriter that errors at 50 KiB and asserts the truncated output: the converted host.go logged Go's own line, `cgi: copy error: past write limit`, and the test passed. What is lost here is the instrument, not the behavior. On windows/amd64 the package has 39 comparable verdicts, 38 matching, this row the only divergence, with Go's side clean.
